newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Rato favours auction of TISA, sees risks.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Rato favours auction of TISA, sees risks.

text.p: Spain's Economy Minister Rodrigo Rato said on Friday he favours auctioning the government's stake in Telefonica Internacional SA (TISA) although this presents some risks.
Rato said Spain could raise between 100 billion ($764 million) and 140 billion pesetas according to an independent firm's valuation of the 23.8 percent stake still in state hands.

Rato cautioned the government has to take into account the risk of a hostile foreign partner getting on to Telefonica's board, and the possibility of a demerger of the Latin America's assets of the company.

"The government has to consider the presence of TISA in Latin America and if the auction could influence this. It has also to consider the possibility that a hostile partner could enter the board," Rato said.
Earlier this week, Spanish press reports said the government will tender its 23.78 percent stake in Telefonica's foreign unit Telefonica Internacional.
A public auction is considered an alternative to selling the stake directly to parent company Telefonica, which owns the rest of the share capital.
